title: Cap. II Arg. 1: Vasquez from Matt. 25:34 — kingdom prepared for foresight works
pass_a_gloss: First, From those words Matt. xxv. 34, &c. Come, ye blessed of the Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world. For I was hungry, and ye gave me, &c. thus Vasquez argues: In this place Christ offers the kingdom prepared from the world's origin, that is, from eternity; and at the same time he renders the reason why they ought to receive the prepared and destined, which is to indicate the cause of the preparation itself. For if the preparation be by another reason, and not on account of these very works which are named, empty and plainly none would be the cause which here Christ himself assigned. Therefore men are elect unto heavenly glory from foresight of their good works. In 1. quest. 23. art. 3. cap. 2. disp. 89. Key lemmas: Matth. xxv. 34; regnum paratum ab initio mundi; causa praeparationis; praevisio operum.
pass_b_english: First argument (Matt. 25:34ff.): "Come, you blessed of the Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the world's beginning. For I was hungry, and you gave me…" Vasquez: here Christ offers a kingdom prepared from the world's origin — that is, from eternity — and at once gives the reason they should receive what was prepared and destined, which is to mark the cause of that preparation. If the preparation rested on some other ground, and not on these very works named, the cause Christ himself assigns would be empty and none. Therefore people are elect to heavenly glory from foresight of their good works (ST I q.23 a.3, disp. 89.2).
source_text: Primo, Ex illis verbis Matth. xxv. 34, &c. Venite benedicti Patris, possidete regnum paratum vobis ab initio mundi. Esurivi enim, & dedistis mihi, &c. sic argumentatur Vasques, Hoc in loco Christus offert regnum praeparatum ab origine mundi, id est, ab aeternitate; atque reddit simul rationem cur debeant accipere praeparatum & destinatum, quod est causam ipsius praeparationis indicare. Nam si praeparatio sit alia ratione, & non propter haec ipsa opera quae nominantur, inanis & nulla plane esset causa quam hic ipse Christus assignavit. Ergo homines eliguntur ad gloriam caelestem ex praevisione operum suorum bonorum. In 1. quaest. 23. art. 3. cap. 2. disp. 89.
